title: Salutation to the Timeless
hook: namastvam akaale: salutation to the One beyond time (Jaap, bhujang prayat)

segments.voice: Yesterday, bhujang prayat, the snake's gait, short, long, long, and your line, glide. Today, the first word of the glide.

Look at your phone's lock screen. On a lot of phones, the biggest thing on it is the time. Not a photo, not a message: the hour and the minute, huge, in the middle. Calendars, deadlines, birthdays, the slow counting of years in a mirror. So much of a day is measured in time, and every clock is counting something down. Now listen to the first word Jaap Sahib salutes when it starts to glide.
screen: `THE BIGGEST THING ON YOUR LOCK SCREEN.` → `THE HOUR AND THE MINUTE.` → `EVERY CLOCK COUNTING SOMETHING DOWN.`

segments.voice: The line is namastvam akaale. Namastvam is two words: namah, a bow, a salutation, and tvam, you. A bow to you. Akaale is the One who is akaal. Open that word. Kaal is time. In Punjabi and the older languages behind it, kaal also means death, because time is the thing that ends us. Put the small a in front, without, and akaal means without time and without death. Timeless and deathless at once. So the first salutation of the glide bows to the One who isn't on the clock at all. Sikhs had met this word long before Jaap. In the Mool Mantar, the opening of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Nanak calls the One akaal moorat, the form beyond time. Sikhs call God Akal Purakh, the Timeless Being. In Amritsar, beside the Golden Temple, stands the Akal Takht, the Throne of the Timeless, which tradition says the sixth Guru, Guru Hargobind, founded. And the word is in the everyday Sikh greeting: Sat Sri Akal. Truth is the Timeless. A whole theology, folded into hello. On an ordinary day, every person you love is in time. Your body is in time. Your worries are in time. Jaap's akaal points to something underneath all of it that the clock can't touch, and Sikhs bow to that first, before anything else in the glide.
screen: `NAMASTVAM: A BOW TO YOU.` · `KAAL: TIME, AND DEATH.` · `AKAAL: TIMELESS, DEATHLESS.` · `SAT SRI AKAL: TRUTH IS THE TIMELESS.` · then, large: `BEYOND TIME.`

segments.voice: Say namastvam akaale three times, slowly, in the snake's rhythm: na-mas-tvam, a-kaa-le. Then turn your phone face down and sit in the quiet that's left, counting nothing, not breaths, not seconds; let time be someone else's job. If you pray, you can rest in the word Akal.
Akaal. Without kaal, without time and without death: the Timeless One, the first salutation of Jaap's glide, and the Akal in Sat Sri Akal.
Your line: beyond time. Not everything that matters is on the clock. Until tomorrow, then.

howItsDone: Sikhs greet one another with Sat Sri Akal, call God Akal Purakh, the Timeless Being, and recite namastvam akaale every morning in Jaap Sahib.
